units.source_text: 源氏内大臣只有正夫人葵姬所生一个儿子夕雾，长得比别人特别俊美，特许在御前和东宫上殿。

en.t: Genji, the Minister of the Interior, had only one son, Yugiri, born to his lawful wife Lady Aoi; the boy was exceptionally handsome, and was specially permitted to attend before the Emperor and the Crown Prince.

units.source_text: 葵姬短命而死，太政大臣和老夫人至今犹有余哀。

en.t: Lady Aoi had died young, and the Grand Minister and his wife still felt the lingering sorrow of her loss.

units.source_text: 然而葵姬逝世后的今日，全靠源氏内大臣的威光而重振家声，多年来的晦气尽行消除，万事欣欣向荣了。

en.t: Yet now, after Lady Aoi's death, the family's name had been restored entirely through Genji's prestige; the ill fortune of many years had vanished, and everything was flourishing.

units.source_text: 源氏内大臣和从前一样，每逢有事，必亲赴太政大臣私邸。

en.t: As before, whenever anything arose, Genji would go in person to the Grand Minister's private residence.

units.source_text: 对于小公子夕雾的乳母及其他侍女，凡这几年来不曾散去的人，每逢适当机会，必然留意照拂。

en.t: As for young Yugiri's nurse and the other ladies in waiting who had not left during these years, he never failed to look after them whenever the occasion allowed.
Because of this, many people saw their fortunes improve.

units.source_text: 二条院方面亦复如是：凡忍苦等待公子归京的人，都蒙公子优遇。

en.t: It was the same at Nijo-in: all those who had endured hardship while waiting for the lord's return to the capital received his generous favor.

units.source_text: 对于中将、中务君等曾蒙宠幸的侍女，适当地加以怜爱，以慰多年来孤寂之苦。

en.t: Toward ladies such as Chujo and Nakatsukasa, who had once enjoyed his affection, he showed suitable tenderness, comforting them for the loneliness they had suffered over the years.

units.source_text: 因此内务多忙，无暇出外游逛了。

en.t: As a result, household affairs kept him so busy that he had no leisure to go out for amusement.

units.source_text: 二条院东面的宫殿，原是桐壶上皇的遗产。

en.t: The palace on the east side of Nijo-in had originally been an inheritance from the retired Emperor Kiritsubo.

units.source_text: 此次大加改筑，壮丽无比。

en.t: It was now extensively rebuilt and became incomparably magnificent.

units.source_text: 为欲使花散里等境况清寒的人住在这里，因而兴工修缮也。

en.t: The work was undertaken so that Hanachirusato and others of modest circumstances could live there.
